LAB_CASES.title: How much should the café prepare?
LAB_CASES.brief: AI proposes two food-prep plans for a campus café.

facts.label: Yesterday
facts.value: 30 lunches sold. The café ran out at noon.

facts.label: Tomorrow
facts.value: A campus event may bring more visitors.

LAB_CASES.task: Which plan would you test first?

choices.benefit: Keeps the food budget and possible leftovers lower.
choices.tradeoff: Walk-in visitors may still find lunch sold out.
choices.check: Count requests you could not serve, not just completed sales.

choices.text: Prepare 40 lunches for the possible rush.
choices.benefit: Leaves room for visitors who did not preorder.
choices.tradeoff: More food may be left over if demand stays low.
choices.check: Track leftovers and agree on an acceptable waste limit.

LAB_CASES.value: See how an AI plan changes when you prioritize cost, food waste or availability.
LAB_CASES.contribution: Set the priorities and test several days of fictional demand.
LAB_CASES.artifact: A spreadsheet showing the plan, demand and outcome.
LAB_CASES.learn: Set useful goals and measure what a sales total misses.
LAB_CASES.career: AI can forecast demand. A business still has to decide what service and waste levels it will accept. Knowing the operation helps you explain those tradeoffs.

LAB_CASES.title: Which image tells the right story?
LAB_CASES.brief: AI helps create two visual directions for a club campaign.

facts.label: One direction
facts.value: Photos from a real student event.

facts.label: Another direction
facts.value: An original AI illustration of the idea.

LAB_CASES.task: Which direction would you develop first?

choices.benefit: Shows the people and experience behind the club.
choices.tradeoff: People may not want their image used in every campaign.
choices.check: Confirm permission for this use with the people pictured.

choices.benefit: Explores a visual idea without depicting actual students.
choices.tradeoff: Viewers could mistake an imagined scene for a real event.
choices.check: Ask viewers what they think it shows and label it clearly.

LAB_CASES.value: Test whether people understand an AI-assisted campaign as intended.
LAB_CASES.contribution: Set the creative direction and review audience feedback and image permissions.
LAB_CASES.artifact: Two mockups, a short creative brief and audience feedback.
LAB_CASES.learn: Guide AI visuals through audience research and editorial decisions.
LAB_CASES.career: As visual production gets faster, designers decide what a campaign represents and whether it fits its audience. A polished image alone cannot settle those choices.

LAB_CASES.title: What would show that a child understands?
LAB_CASES.brief: AI designs two activities for children learning to count.

facts.label: What you notice
facts.value: Some children get the answer but cannot explain it.

facts.label: Your goal
facts.value: Find out whether they understand the idea.

LAB_CASES.task: Which activity would you try first?

choices.text: Give each learner adaptive AI practice.
choices.benefit: Adjusts the pace and examples for each learner.
choices.tradeoff: Correct screen answers may not show how the learner is thinking.
choices.check: Ask the learner to explain a new example without the tool.

choices.text: Try an AI-planned group activity with objects.
choices.benefit: Makes reasoning and different strategies visible.
choices.tradeoff: A confident child may do most of the talking.
choices.check: Give every learner a turn to show their own approach.

LAB_CASES.value: Compare what learners understand afterward, not just how many answers they complete.
LAB_CASES.contribution: Define a learning goal and review both activities with an educator.
LAB_CASES.artifact: Two activity plans and an observation checklist. Begin with adult role-play.
LAB_CASES.learn: Choose evidence that shows learning beyond task completion.
LAB_CASES.career: AI can generate lessons and personalize practice. Educators need to decide what learning looks like and notice when a child needs another approach.

LAB_CASES.title: Will people be able to use the information?
LAB_CASES.brief: AI drafts appointment information in several languages.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Some people have limited data or share a phone.

facts.label: Information
facts.value: A short reminder and detailed preparation instructions.

LAB_CASES.task: Which approach would you test first?

choices.text: Send a short reminder with a number to call.
choices.benefit: Works without a portal login or a long download.
choices.tradeoff: People need another step to get the full instructions.
choices.check: Test whether people know what to do next and can reach support.

choices.text: Link to a detailed, translated portal guide.
choices.benefit: Keeps the instructions together with room for explanation.
choices.tradeoff: Login or data access may prevent people from reading it.
choices.check: Test the login and guide with volunteers using different devices and languages.

LAB_CASES.value: Test whether people can act on accurate information in the way it is delivered.
LAB_CASES.contribution: Map the reader’s steps and test understanding with fictional notices.
LAB_CASES.artifact: Two message prototypes and notes from a small usability test.
LAB_CASES.learn: Evaluate access, privacy and understanding together.
LAB_CASES.career: Even accurate AI writing has to work for the person receiving it. Health teams need people who can connect communication tools with actual patient workflows.

LAB_CASES.title: Where should the next measurement go?
LAB_CASES.brief: AI turns a small temperature dataset into a campus heat map.

facts.label: Limited time
facts.value: You can collect one more set of measurements.

LAB_CASES.task: Which evidence would you collect next?

choices.benefit: Shows whether areas are missing from the map.
choices.tradeoff: One afternoon still cannot show how conditions change.
choices.check: Record shade, surface and measurement time consistently.

choices.text: Measure the busiest route at several times.
choices.benefit: Shows how conditions change where many people walk.
choices.check: Compare the model’s predictions with the repeated readings.

LAB_CASES.value: Test how sampling choices change an AI map and what people can use it for.
LAB_CASES.contribution: Choose measurement locations, document conditions and check predictions.
LAB_CASES.artifact: A small dataset, a map and a clear statement of its limits.
LAB_CASES.learn: Plan data collection around the decision a model will support.
LAB_CASES.career: AI can fit models and summarize results. Scientists and engineers need evidence from the setting where a result will be used, and a reason for collecting it.

LAB_CASES.title: What will help readers take the next step?
LAB_CASES.brief: AI produces two accurate translations of a community notice.

facts.label: Original
facts.value: Formal wording with unfamiliar service names.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Readers who need to find the right service quickly.

LAB_CASES.task: Which version would you test with readers first?

choices.text: Keep the wording close to the original.
choices.benefit: Makes it easier to compare the translation with the source.
choices.tradeoff: Formal terms may still be difficult for new readers.
choices.check: Ask readers to identify the next action without help.

choices.text: Use plain language with short explanations.
choices.benefit: Explains unfamiliar terms in the reader’s context.
choices.tradeoff: Editing can shift emphasis or hide useful distinctions.
choices.check: Ask bilingual reviewers to check meaning and readers to test the instructions.

LAB_CASES.value: Test whether an accurate translation helps its intended audience take action.
LAB_CASES.contribution: Explain audience needs and review meaning, tone and understanding.
LAB_CASES.artifact: Two versions of a public notice and a short reader-test summary.
LAB_CASES.learn: Check both accuracy and practical understanding.
LAB_CASES.career: As translation and drafting improve, language professionals can shape how information is understood in a specific community. Knowing the audience is part of the work.

LAB_CASES.title: The agent can make the change. May it?
LAB_CASES.brief: An AI coding agent prepares a fix that passes the project’s automated tests.

facts.label: Capability
facts.value: The agent can edit, test and deploy code.

facts.label: Responsibility
facts.value: Your team sets its permissions and release rules.

LAB_CASES.task: Which permission model would you pilot?

choices.text: Have it prepare changes for approval.
choices.benefit: A reviewer sees each change before it is released.
choices.tradeoff: Routine fixes wait when reviewers are busy.
choices.check: Give reviewers a clear change summary and evidence beyond “tests passed.”

choices.text: Allow a narrow set of reversible releases.
choices.benefit: Routine work can move without approval for every step.
choices.tradeoff: A mistake can reach users before someone reviews it.
choices.check: Define allowed changes, access limits, monitoring and when to roll back.

LAB_CASES.value: Explore how a capable agent works with different permissions and recovery rules.
LAB_CASES.contribution: Define permitted actions and test what happens outside those limits.
LAB_CASES.artifact: A small test repository, an action log and a rollback demonstration.
LAB_CASES.learn: Design permissions and recovery as part of an AI system.
LAB_CASES.career: As agents work more independently, software teams need people who can decide what they may change and how to recover. Working code is only one part of a reliable release.

LAB_CASES.title: Who gets a place when seats are limited?
LAB_CASES.brief: AI can schedule a free workshop using either admission plan.

facts.label: Access
facts.value: Some people book online; others rely on walk-ins.

LAB_CASES.task: Which plan would you discuss with the service team?

choices.benefit: More people know they have a place before traveling.
choices.tradeoff: People without online access have fewer places available.
choices.check: Track empty reservations and people turned away at the door.

choices.benefit: Leaves more room for people who cannot book online.
choices.tradeoff: More visitors travel without knowing whether a seat remains.
choices.check: Ask about booking barriers and make the admission plan clear.

LAB_CASES.value: Show how a booking rule affects different ways people access a service.
LAB_CASES.contribution: Identify who each rule helps or excludes and test fictional attendance patterns.
LAB_CASES.artifact: Two booking rules, simulated outcomes and questions for a community partner.
LAB_CASES.learn: Turn access goals into rules that can be reviewed and changed.
LAB_CASES.career: AI can apply a policy consistently without deciding whether it serves the community well. Public-service teams need evidence, public input and a way to review the outcome.

LAB_CASES.title: What would prove the plan works on site?
LAB_CASES.brief: AI proposes an HVAC schedule that uses less energy in a building simulation.

facts.label: Model
facts.value: Assumes a typical day and typical room occupancy.

facts.label: Building
facts.value: Weather, equipment and room use change.

LAB_CASES.task: Which test would you plan first?

choices.text: Test more conditions in the simulator.
choices.benefit: Explores hot days and busy rooms without changing a real system.
choices.tradeoff: The simulator may still miss a condition in the building.
choices.check: Compare its assumptions with equipment records and measured conditions.

choices.text: Plan a supervised trial in one suitable space.
choices.benefit: Shows how the plan works with the actual equipment and room.
choices.tradeoff: A poor change can affect comfort or operation during the trial.
choices.check: Have the responsible professional set limits, monitoring and a stop condition.

LAB_CASES.value: Connect AI recommendations with the measurements and limits of a real building.
LAB_CASES.contribution: Review a fictional system’s assumptions and plan what to measure before a change.
LAB_CASES.artifact: An instructor-reviewed test plan using simulated data.
LAB_CASES.learn: Connect model results with physical conditions and operating limits.
LAB_CASES.career: As AI improves design and scheduling, trades professionals need to verify the installed system and its conditions. This helps turn a recommendation into an accountable site decision.

LAB_SOURCES.note: Informs our focus on context, evaluation and contributions from domain experts, users and affected communities.

LAB_WORK_SOURCES.note: Explore how AI could affect the mix of tasks within an occupation. These are estimates of potential exposure, not observed job losses or a forecast of your career.

LAB_WORK_SOURCES.title: Canaries Dashboard
LAB_WORK_SOURCES.note: Explore employment trends by occupation, age and AI exposure using payroll data. A change in employment does not, by itself, establish that AI caused it.

LAB_WORK_SOURCES.title: Economic Index: work and AI use
LAB_WORK_SOURCES.note: See the tasks people bring to Claude, from reports and marketing to code and translation. These are usage patterns and user experiences, not a count of jobs replaced.

LAB_WORK_SOURCES.title: AI exposure and career outlook
LAB_WORK_SOURCES.note: Look up an occupation’s AI exposure alongside the 2025–35 employment projections. Exposure describes how tasks relate to AI capabilities and use; it is not a prediction of job loss.
